subject: Packaging decision: pilot tier & feature bundling for PulseWorks
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@pulseworks.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pack selection for pilot – Compact vs Throughput

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're trying to lock down packaging for the pilot with Redwood. A couple of constraints that matter for the business case:
- Expected steady-state: ~12k tokens/min (all gen requests), peak bursts up to ~60k tokens/min during batch processing windows.
- P95 latency target for interactive flows: <350ms.
- Need embeddings for search (small volume) and a reranking path for top-K.

Two internal stakeholders are aligned on a conservative start (lower cost) but engineering is pushing for fewer latency surprises during bursts. Could you recommend which tier/pack we should start with and whether to bundle any add-ons (burst capacity, dedicated KV caching, per-route priority)?

Attaching a usage snapshot to help sizing.

Appreciate quick guidance — we have a procurement review next week.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Product, PulseWorks
Attachment: PW-usage-snapshot.csv (csv)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@pulseworks.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pack selection for pilot – Compact vs Throughput

Lena — thanks for the snapshot, this is helpful. High level guidance below then a recommended MAP (mutual action plan).

Options (tradeoffs):
1) Compact (cost-efficient):
  - Suggested for pilots with predictable, lower sustained throughput. Includes token meter pricing and standard caching.
  - Pros: lower unit cost; lower monthly commitment.
  - Cons: higher chance of transient latency when bursts exceed pooled capacity.

2) High-Throughput (dedicated/dedicated-pool):
  - Suggested if you expect frequent sustained bursts or strict latency SLOs. Includes dedicated GPU pool, priority routing, and KV caching options.
  - Pros: predictable latency and throughput; easier autoscale policies.
  - Cons: higher committed cost.

Bundling suggestion: Start on Compact + Burst Add-on (1–2 burst GPUs) + Embeddings bundle. On signal of sustained 30%+ sustained above baseline for 48h, roll to Dedicated pool. We can include a temporary 3-month discounted add-on to smooth the migration.

Pricing/discount note: Ben will propose two pricing bands (monthly vs annual commit). For pilots we often do a 10–15% pilot discount depending on term/usage.

Proposed MAP:
- Today: Redwood sends draft quote + recommended config (Ben).
- Tue: PulseWorks confirms target pilot dates and acceptance criteria (Lena).
- Wed: Redwood provides canary config and MOU for pilot (Marissa).

I cc'd Ben for concrete pricing.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@pulseworks.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T15:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pack selection for pilot – Compact vs Throughput

Lena — quick pricing and options from my side.

1) Compact + Burst Add-on (recommended starting point)
  - Baseline: metered tokens at $0.0008 / token (generation) + $100/month embeddings bundle (small volume).
  - Burst Add-on: $1200/month for 2x burst GPUs (billed monthly pro rata).
  - Pilot discount: 12% off baseline for a 3-month pilot, or 18% off if you sign a 12-month commit that we can apply mid-pilot.

2) High-Throughput (Dedicated pool)
  - Reserved pool pricing starts at $8k/month for a 4-GPU pool with autoscale credit buckets.
  - If committed annually, we can offer a 20% discount and include 10% free burst credits for the first quarter.

Notes:
- We can include a one-time migration credit (equivalent to one month of burst add-on) if you commit to a 12-month plan within 60 days of pilot start.
- Draft quote attached (PDF) with line-item SKUs and prorate examples.

Next step: I can prepare two clean quotations (pilot SKU with 3-month discount, and annual-commit SKU) for procurement. Which path should I finalize?

Attachment: PW-draft-quote.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@pulseworks.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T01:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pack selection for pilot – Compact vs Throughput

Quick technical addendum from infra:

- The usage snapshot implies a working set where KV cache hit-rate will materially affect latency during bursts. If you keep embeddings/rerank on the same instance class, KV pinning will reduce P95 by ~120–180ms for those flows.
- Compact + Burst is fine for initial pilot; please set the burst policy to 95th-percentile scaling (aggressive) for the first two weeks to collect realistic telemetry.
- If you see sustained >50 req/s for longer than 24 hours we strongly recommend moving to Dedicated to avoid queuing. Dedicated also enables quantization-friendly kernels that reduce GPU memory and can improve throughput by ~15%.

I'll help define the canary configuration (exact GPU type, kv_cache size, batch limits) once PulseWorks confirms target days.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@pulseworks.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: PulseWorks Procurement <procurement@pulseworks.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T10:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pack selection for pilot – Compact vs Throughput

Thanks, team. PulseWorks prefers to start on Compact + Burst Add-on with the 3-month pilot discount and the milestone to evaluate a roll to Dedicated if telemetry shows sustained load. Please proceed with the pilot quote (we need the formal numbers for procurement review).

Procurement: please review the attached sample and we will need standard redlines (payment terms, data deletion clause).

Lena Ortiz
Head of Product, PulseWorks
